note: Executed against a DISPOSABLE COPY of the dev sqlite DB (deleted after). Proves the tenant-scoping PRIMITIVE: the scoped {id,companyId} filter isolates tenants, while an unscoped findUnique/update by raw id crosses tenants — so every loader/writer MUST add the companyId/allowedClubIds filter (ARCH-005). The static scanners (security-read/write-scope.json) inventory whether each real site does.

results.desc: A reads B's club via {id, companyId:A} scoped filter
raw findUnique({id}) WITHOUT companyId returns B's row (demonstrates the scope filter is load-bearing — ARCH-005)
results.detail: raw id read returned B's row → any unscoped loader leaks

results.desc: A's club list (companyId=A, id in allowedClubIds=[clubA]) never contains clubB
A writes B's club via updateMany({id, companyId:A}) affects 0 rows
raw updateMany({id}) WITHOUT companyId matches B's row (a mass-assignment/unguarded write would cross tenants)
results.detail: raw id write matched 1 row → unguarded id-keyed writes are cross-tenant capable
